description: A series of 8–10 parallel, low-relief embankments and intervening channels, spaced ~20–30 m apart, trending NE–SW across a gentle interfluve slope. The ridge crests reach ~0.5 m above the surrounding terrain, while the adjacent troughs are ~0.3 m deep. These alignments are not correlated with any modern roads or clearings on OSM and coincide with moisture-retaining patterns in the NIR imagery, consistent with pre-Columbian raised-field agriculture.

A sinuous linear depression ~1.2 km long and ~3–4 m wide, oriented NE–SW, cutting across natural contour lines. It exhibits a consistent depth of ~0.4 m in the DTM curvature maps and corresponds to a moisture anomaly in the NIR band, suggesting an ancient canal or feeder ditch. No matching feature appears in the OSM layer, and it terminates upslope of a minor seasonal stream.

An east-west oriented causeway–like embankment ~300 m long and ~5 m wide, showing pronounced convex curvature in the hillshade derivative and low curvature values in surrounding terrain. The feature is uplifted ~0.6 m above adjacent ground and displays a subtle NIR reflectance signature of higher moisture retention, typical of compacted anthropogenic substrate.
